A.claim: If a Beal counterexample exists, one exists with all three exponents in {4} union {odd primes}; equivalently the signature-by-signature strategy is legitimate.

B.claim: A Beal counterexample with all three exponents even is exactly a primitive Pythagorean triple (A^r, B^s, C^t) whose entries are perfect powers with r,s,t >= 2.

combine.instructions: Would combining these two candidates produce a genuinely NEW attack (not a reword of either)?
criteria: level 2: a concrete new lemma or test could be written
level 3: the combination could close an infinite family

shared_failure.instructions: Do they share the SAME failure mode (so combining cannot help)?
